newsitem.title: MEXICO: Hylsamex sees year-end sales volume up.
newsitem.headline: Hylsamex sees year-end sales volume up.

text.p: Mexican steel firm Hylsamex, a unit of conglomerate Grupo Industrial Alfa estimates that its sales volume will end the year up 12-15 percent over sales in 1995, a company director said in an interview.

"Last year, we produced 2.14 million tonnes of finished product and for 1996 we would be thinking of a growth rate of between 12 and 15 percent," Rafael Rubio, the director of economic studies and international marketing said.
Hylsamex takes it as a given that its finished product volumes convert into sales volumes.

Rubio said national demand for steel could grow between 15 percent and 20 percent in 1996 over 1995, but he added "that number is deceptive because we're talking about seven million tonnes (of domestic consumption) in 1995 against 13 million tonnes in 1994."
Rubio said exports would make up about 20 percent to 25 percent of Hylsamex's production in 1996 compared to 28 percent in 1995.
He attributed this change in part to lower prices on the international market.
"For 1997, if the Mexican economy continues getting stronger, we're going to orient ourselves to the national market," Rubio said.
How aggressively Hylsamex pursues the export market in 1997 will depend largely on international prices, he said.
"If they remain at current levels at least, there could be some attraction," Rubio said.
But if world prices dip lower Hylsamex would "limit by plenty" its exports, he said. --Daniel Perez, Monterrey
